sections.description: Update installs now use the approved non-blocking pill and decision ledger, and Theme Styles edge controls stay contained in narrow panels.
sections.changelog:
v1.3.500 — Update dock visual pass and Media Studio font uploads

  • Rebuilt the update install dock to the approved Variant D visual pass. Depth now comes from surface lightness rather than outlines, so the pill and ledger sit above the builder canvas instead of reading flat against it, and the release-notes block recesses inside the ledger holding it.
  • Reduced the dock to the MV type ramp: three sizes (13/11.5/10) and two weights (400/600), replacing seven sizes and weights up to 900. The only edges left are the eight step dots, where the border is the control.
  • Moved success and failure signalling onto the progress ring alone, so the accent marks state and nothing else. Renamed the final install stage from “Refreshing update caches” to “Finishing up”.
  • Allowed font files (WOFF2, WOFF, TTF, OTF) to be uploaded through Media Studio. WordPress permits no font type in the media library, so every font dropped on a Fonts collection was rejected before it could become an attachment. Scoped to Media Studio uploads by a user who may already upload files, and every file is checked against its format signature.
  • Made a failed upload state its reason. The toast reported “0 uploaded · 2 failed” and discarded the message WordPress had returned, leaving the cause invisible; it now shows the reason and stays until dismissed.

v1.3.499 — Update decision dock and contained Quiet cross

  • Routine plugin installs stay in a corner progress pill; failures and successful installs open a named step ledger only when a decision is needed.
  • Successful installs show current release notes and require an explicit Reload the builder or Later choice. The builder never reloads automatically.
  • Theme Styles T/R/B/L controls now share one responsive width, so equal fields shrink together instead of escaping narrow panels.

v1.3.498 — Complete Quiet cross parity

  • All four Theme Styles edge inputs now use the same width while the quiet centre absorbs the remaining panel space.
  • The resting value and unit are separate; focus merges them for direct unit typing without duplicate text.
  • Unit-aware scrubbing, value fill, keyboard finish, explicit px/rem/em/%/vw/vh selection and linked propagation now match the approved prototype.

v1.3.497 — Quiet cross and Calendar Unscheduled rail

  • Theme Styles box controls now use the approved quiet centre with direct T/R/B/L typing, scrubbing, unit selection and linked editing.
  • Content Studio Calendar now keeps drafts with no target date in an Unscheduled rail beside month and week views.
  • Dragging an unscheduled draft onto a day stores explicit target-date intent, while scheduled WordPress posts remain in Content Studio queries.

v1.3.496 — Disabled modules stay disabled after delayed settings responses

  • Older App-level settings responses can no longer repaint the rail after a newer module toggle.
  • Settings mutation events consume their saved response directly, while payload-less fallbacks are revision-guarded.
  • The console module-state helper now reports the runtime revision for future diagnostics.

v1.3.495 — Immediate module state and a working maintenance handoff

  • Settings module switches update the current Admin or Builder rail before cross-window and server reconciliation, so enabling a module no longer waits for refresh.
  • Bricks Settings’ Open Site Visibility button switches directly into Unified Settings → Site Visibility on first and later opens.

v1.3.494 — CSS Studio can close and the shared picker stays canonical

  • CSS Studio’s unsaved-change confirmation stays above its backdrop and panel, so backdrop and header-close requests can be completed without a refresh.
  • Content Studio no longer overrides the shared colour picker’s segmented format controls or selected state.

v1.3.493 — Shared autocomplete and reliable module switches

  • Theme Styles, CSS Studio, CSS Recipes and every MV CSS editor now share one preloaded autocomplete index.
  • Suggestion data refreshes after variable changes without duplicate concurrent requests.
  • Admin and Builder module switches apply an atomic surface-specific update, so CSS Recipes can be enabled immediately without disturbing the other rail.

v1.3.492 — Public framework variables return to autocomplete

  • Variables explicitly registered in Bricks/Advanced Themer, Core Framework and Automatic.css are suggested alongside MV and CSS Studio variables.
  • Provider variables retain their literal CSS names without migration-family merging.
  • Arbitrary provider settings and internal plugin/theme implementation styles remain excluded.

v1.3.491 — Autocomplete and migration use separate indexes

  • Normal suggestions contain Mimam's Var variables and CSS Studio declarations, not Bricks, Advanced Themer or migration-provider framework variables.
  • User-authored Bricks global classes remain available while Advanced Themer framework classes are excluded by structured provenance.
  • CSS Studio custom-property names retain their first character during normalization.

v1.3.490 — Bricks suggestions use explicit authored stores

  • Server autocomplete reads only Bricks global classes, global variables and theme styles rather than every bricks_% option.
  • Unrelated Bricks settings can no longer contribute implementation variable, class or ID names.

v1.3.489 — Autocomplete indexes authored site names only

  • Live CSS resolves the effective value of a known variable without contributing new names.
  • WordPress admin, theme, plugin, Bricks and MV interface implementation variables, classes and IDs no longer enter autocomplete from the current DOM or loaded stylesheets.
  • Generated framework CSS, theme/plugin source and templates, taxonomy slugs, generic plugin options and third-party snippet tables are excluded from the server index.

v1.3.488 — Autocomplete stays inside the editor and suggests usable variables

  • Suggestion menus remain within the owning CodeMirror rectangle instead of crossing its borders.
  • MV interface styling tokens are excluded from site/design-variable autocomplete.
  • Reference-only and unresolved names are removed, so every variable suggestion has an authored or live value.

v1.3.487 — Autocomplete is stable, contextual, and viewport-safe

  • The active completion now filters in place instead of closing and reopening on every keystroke.
  • Property, value, and variable menus share one width, stay inside the viewport, and never scroll horizontally.
  • Variables appear only after --, var, or var(; ordinary value typing suggests CSS values.
  • MV and detected external variables carry authored/live values and sources, with defined variables ranked before reference-only names.

v1.3.486 — Hidden autocomplete lists are restored

Live Firefox console evidence showed the correct CodeMirror list was computed as display:none with a 0×0 rectangle. MV now forces the active list to display before positioning it and reports hidden states directly instead of falsely blaming the studio backdrop.

v1.3.485 — Autocomplete uses a root-level viewport portal

Replaced the live-failing Popover API path with one direct-body fixed portal for CodeMirror suggestions. The active editor widget's own list is positioned beside the caret, remains hit-testable above MV's studio backdrop, and can be inspected through mimamVarInspectAutocomplete().

v1.3.484 — Autocomplete suggestions appear beside the caret

Fixed the live top-layer positioning conflict that collapsed the generated suggestion list into a thin strip at the top of the viewport. Theme Styles and other MV CodeMirror editors now place the list beside the caret above the studio backdrop. The failure message no longer blames another plugin for an MV-owned display problem.

v1.3.483 — The suggestion list renders in the browser top layer

Three builds were spent trying to make the list out-rank button.ve-studio-backdrop, MV’s own full-viewport blurred layer behind an open studio panel. It carries a backdrop-filter, which makes it a compositing root, and nothing outside one reliably paints above it — not a maximum z-index, not moving the list last in the document, not hosting it inside the panel. Each attempt was a different way of losing the same argument.

The list now renders in the browser’s top layer, which is not part of that argument at all: it paints above every stacking context on the page regardless of z-index, ancestry or filters. It is positioned at the caret in viewport terms, and browsers without top-layer support fall back to the previous behaviour.

v1.3.482 — The suggestion list moves inside the panel

The diagnostics named the culprit: button.ve-studio-backdrop — MV’s own full-viewport backdrop, the blurred layer behind an open studio panel. It carries a backdrop-filter, and an element with one forms its own compositing root. A suggestion list parked at the end of the page body does not reliably paint above that no matter how large its z-index is, which is why raising it repeatedly changed nothing.

The list is now hosted by the panel that owns the editor. The panel is already drawn above the backdrop, so there is no contest left to win. The container is also hit-testable again — making it transparent to the mouse had been quietly breaking the very check that found this.

v1.3.481 — Lift the suggestion list clear of whatever covers it

The previous build proved what was wrong: the suggestions were being built and opened, then painted over. Raising the list’s z-index was not enough on its own — a competing overlay can sit at the maximum too, and on a tie the element later in the document wins, so simply having a big number does not settle it.

The list is now lifted two ways at once: to the top of the stacking range, and to the end of the document, which also takes it out of any ancestor stacking context it could not otherwise escape. If something still manages to cover it, the panel names that element outright rather than describing it vaguely, so the culprit can be dealt with directly.

v1.3.480 — The suggestion list can no longer hide behind the panel

Sitting in the right place is not the same as being visible. The list was being built correctly and positioned correctly, and MV checked only its coordinates — so a list painted underneath the panel was recorded as shown. From the outside that is identical to nothing happening, which is exactly what it looked like.

MV now asks the page what is actually on top at the list’s position. If something is over it, the list is lifted clear; if it stays covered, the panel says so instead of staying quiet. The list also outranks every MV surface by default rather than sitting just above the panel.

v1.3.479 — A suggestion request can no longer end in silence

Four different things can leave the suggestion list empty — the caret being somewhere no suggestion applies, nothing having been collected to suggest from, nothing matching what you typed, or the list opening correctly but somewhere off-screen. From the outside all four look identical: you type, and nothing happens. That is why this took so many rounds to pin down.

Each cause is now named underneath the editor. A list that opens outside the viewport is re-anchored to the caret, flipping above it when there is no room below. And if suggestions are produced but never reach the page, the panel says exactly that rather than staying quiet.

v1.3.478 — MV pins its own CodeMirror

window.CodeMirror is shared ground and whichever plugin loads last owns it. This site runs Code2Bricks, which ships its own build. MV read that global at the moment it created an editor — so if the build in place had no autocomplete addon, the editor still mounted and looked completely normal while every attempt to open the suggestion list threw inside a timer, where nothing surfaced it. A real editor that silently never suggested anything.

MV now takes a reference to the build it has verified and uses that from then on, whatever the global becomes afterwards. Every hint call is guarded, and when one cannot open the panel says why underneath the editor instead of leaving you to guess.

v1.3.477 — Every code editor is MV’s own CodeMirror

MV decided whether to give you a real code editor by scanning the page for a <link> tag whose URL mentioned CodeMirror. If the guess came out false it silently swapped in a plain textarea that still drew line numbers and syntax colours — so it looked like the real editor while offering no suggestions, and which one you got depended on what else the host page happened to load.

MV ships its own CodeMirror, so it now loads it when the page has none instead of guessing and degrading. Another plugin’s CodeMirror stylesheet no longer counts as MV’s — it is unscoped and would fight over MV’s editors. The textarea is reached only if MV’s own bundled files cannot be fetched at all, and when that happens the panel now says so under the editor rather than leaving you to wonder.

v1.3.476 — Module toggles apply immediately

Module switches could appear to work, then reverse when the Settings request that opened the panel finished with older data. Rapid changes could also start from a stale render, while event senders guessed whether each discovered window was an Admin or Builder surface. Settings now guards older reads with a mutation revision, keeps a synchronous state snapshot for rapid toggles, and broadcasts the complete module state so every receiving runtime resolves its own surface. The matching rail updates immediately without a refresh.

v1.3.475 — Suggestions in wp-admin, and a box control that survives the pinned rail

The suggestion list never appeared in wp-admin. CodeMirror positions its hints by subtracting the container’s offset from page-relative cursor coordinates, and MV’s container had no CSS at all — so the result depended entirely on the host page. On the short Bricks canvas it landed correctly; on a long scrolling admin screen it landed far above the viewport. The container is now pinned to the viewport origin, which makes the offset zero and the position identical everywhere.

The box control was laid out with absolute insets sized for a 410px panel with the group rail collapsed. Pin the rail open and the body loses about 100px: the bands collapsed below a field width, the element ended up narrower than the inputs around it and the right-hand field spilled outside the dashed edge. It is now a three-by-three grid sized from what is actually available, so it cannot break at any panel width, with more room around it. The centre caption also said “ALL” for element margins — an internal grouping token, not a name for anything on the page.

v1.3.474 — Box control, picker card, shared suggestions

The box control in Bricks Theme Styles was four inputs arranged around a label, which never answered “spacing of what?”. It now draws the thing it edits: the hatched band is the spacing, the solid rectangle is the element, and each field sits on the band it controls.

The highlight colour picker had no card at all. An earlier fix for a double frame removed both frames — the popover wrapper and the picker’s own — leaving the controls floating on the editor. The core keeps its card, matching the Component Library, and a check now requires every picker host to show exactly one.

The Theme Styles stylesheet editor was built with only the variables already in memory, so it never saw the server-side class, id and selector scan the CSS Studio editors get. Same editor, different suggestions depending on where you opened it. Every CodeMirror in MV now shares one pool.

v1.3.473 — Light mode reaches the whole colour picker

Switching Content Studio to Light left parts of the highlight colour picker dark. Rather than fix the one rule that was reported, every picker declaration carrying a dark-only colour was enumerated and given a light counterpart: the trigger swatch and each variable swatch had an alpha checkerboard mixed for a dark ground, the alpha percentage box had a light rule for its text but not its fill, and the bound-variable chip used a pale lime that vanished on light. One of them could not win at all — Content Studio scopes those swatch borders with !important, which outranked the light rule regardless of source order. A regression check now walks the whole picker and fails if any element gains a dark-only colour without a light counterpart for that same property.

v1.3.472 — Suggestion values and per-control history

The CSS Studio suggestion list showed variable names only, so you had to already know what a token held before you could pick one. Every variable now carries a preview matched to its kind (colour on a checkerboard so alpha reads, a proportional bar for a length, real letterforms for a font stack), its resolved value as text, and a badge naming where it is defined — MV, Theme Styles, Bricks or a page stylesheet. An alias shows its chain then the final value; a circular reference is reported rather than resolved; an undefined token says so instead of showing a guess.

Bricks Theme Styles gained undo, redo and clear on every control, plus the same three for a whole group. History is per setting, so undoing a colour cannot revert a font size changed after it, and a burst of typing collapses into one step rather than one per keystroke. Clear removes the value entirely so the Bricks default returns.

v1.3.471 — Variable menu stacking

Each colour row’s ⚡ wrapper carried a z-index, which makes it a stacking context. The open menu’s own high z-index only ranked it inside that one row, so every row further down the panel — same z-index, later in the DOM — painted its ⚡ straight through the open list. The wrapper itself now lifts while its menu is open, so the whole subtree clears the rows below.

v1.3.470 — Selected recent ring

The ring was a box-shadow painted 2px outside the swatch, and the picker core clips — overflow:hidden, with its padding removed inside a popover — so the outer edge was cut. It is now an outline with a negative offset, drawn inside the swatch’s own box: impossible to clip, no layout cost, with an inset hairline so it stays visible on a swatch close to the brand colour.

v1.3.469 — When a colour becomes “recent”

It was recorded only when you typed a hex — so dragging the map, the hue or the alpha recorded nothing, which is most of how the picker is actually used. A colour is now remembered on close, once per picker session, and only if it changed.

Not on every edit: a drag emits hundreds of intermediate colours nobody chose. Not only on a typed hex: that is the rarest way anyone picks. The distinction is a colour you used versus one you passed through on the way to it. Alpha is kept, so a translucent colour comes back translucent.

v1.3.468 — Hue stays a rainbow; popover stays put

  • The hue slider no longer greys while you drag. Exempting ranges from the control-height rules missed two more — including .ve-row input:focus. A slider takes focus on pointer-down, which is precisely why it only greyed mid-drag. Ranges are exempt from those too, and the hue and alpha gradients now carry !important so no host rule can repaint them.
  • The popover stays inside the panel as it grows. The clamp was writing style.top, but the host renders left/top from state — so every re-render, including each keystroke in the VAR search, wiped the correction and it slid back off the bottom. It now nudges with transform, which the host does not manage.

v1.3.467 — Popover keeps itself in bounds; Variables picker closes

  • The popover re-clamps as it grows. It was measured once when it opened, so switching to VAR — which adds a variable list — made it taller after the decision had been taken, and it hung off the bottom of the panel again. It now clamps on open and on every resize, and scrolls internally when taller than its container. The Theme Styles popover had the same staleness choosing which way to open.
  • The Variables colour picker closes on an outside click or Escape. It only ever toggled from its own swatch, so once open the only way out was to click that swatch again.

v1.3.466 — The colour sliders, root cause

.ve-sr input, .ve-row input and .ve-ren input force every descendant input to the 38px control height with !important — right for text and number fields, wrong for a range slider. The Variables panel is the only host that wraps the picker in .ve-row, which is exactly why its two sliders rendered at 38px while every other picker looked correct, and why the track’s own height:14px never applied: no !important, so it lost on specificity.

Ranges are now exempt from those three rules, and the track asserts its own height so a future host cannot override it the same way.

v1.3.465 — Alpha slider, measured this time

Two separate causes, both now measured rather than guessed. The % readout was 20px while the hue row is 18px — that row’s height comes from its thumb, not its 14px track — so the alpha block always stood taller. And the track reused the same 10px, 20%-contrast checkerboard as the 34px swatches, which inside a 14px bar is 1.4 rows of loud squares: it read as a block, not a slider.

The readout is now 18px so both rows match exactly, and the track checker is 6px at 4% contrast — texture rather than pattern. Light mode too. Two checks pin both so neither can drift back.

v1.3.464 — Transparency slider connected

  • The slider does something now. Theme Styles passed the picker a fixed alpha:1 and an empty change handler, so it rendered, dragged, reported nothing, and snapped back to 100%. Alpha is read from and written to the stored value as an eight-digit hex, which Bricks resolves straight into CSS.
  • The swatch shows translucency — the colour is layered over a checkerboard rather than replacing it, so half-transparent no longer looks opaque.
  • Two checks now reject a no-op alpha handler or a hard-coded alpha:1 in any picker host.

v1.3.463 — Colour popover fits the pinned rail

The popover was a fixed 316px. That fitted the old full-width body, but pinning the new group rail leaves only about 270px (468 − 150 − padding), so it overflowed and the panel scrolled sideways. It now anchors to its field row and is exactly as wide as the space available — at any rail width.

v1.3.462 — Rail icons, actually fixed

A Phosphor icon is a font glyph drawn on a ::before pseudo-element. I had put display:grid on the <i>, which turns that pseudo into a grid item and lets the default line-height inflate the box — so every glyph rendered low and read as two marks stacked above its label. MV’s own studio tool rail already had this right: flex-centre the button, and give the icon nothing but a size and line-height:1. The group rail now matches it, and the contract check rejects display:grid on a glyph so it cannot return.

v1.3.461 — Rail cleanup

  • The stray squares are gone. The set-dot is an <i>, and the rail’s icon rule matched every <i> in a button — so each dot was sized as a 19px icon box. Scoped to the glyph.
  • No more doubled label. Rail buttons carried a native tooltip repeating the name the rail already shows on hover.
  • Hover fits the longest group name. Overlaying costs nothing underneath, so hover is as wide as the text needs; only the pinned width stays fixed at 150px and truncates, because that width is taken out of the fields.

v1.3.460 — Theme Styles groups move to a rail

  • All ten groups visible at once. They never fitted across 410px, so six were always scrolled out of sight — including the set-dots marking which groups hold values. The rail shows every one in 52px.
  • Hover reveals the names, the pin keeps them. Labels slide out as an overlay so the fields underneath never reflow; pinning reserves 150px permanently. The choice is remembered, and it starts collapsed.
  • Added to the Component Library as Panel group rail before porting, so the next panel with too many groups — Bricks Settings has more — has something to adopt rather than reinvent.

v1.3.459 — Repairing what v1.3.458 broke

  • The transparency slider works again. Pinning its height with a flex-basis set its width instead, because it sits in a flex row — it collapsed to a dot. That change had also overridden the alpha row from its intended grid to flex. Both reverted.
  • The height reported twice is fixed. The alpha row was 30px because of the percentage readout, against a 14px hue bar above it, so the block looked twice as tall. Both now share one rhythm.
  • The Media Studio popover clipping is fixed. It is position:fixed, but a backdrop-filter ancestor makes the studio its containing block — so it can never escape the panel, and clamping it to the window pushed it under the panel edge. It clamps inside the panel again, using its measured height, and scrolls internally if taller than the panel.
  • Added three regression checks for exactly these mistakes, each verified to fail when the bug is put back.

v1.3.458 — Recent colours, one frame, nothing clipped

  • Recently used colours replace the fixed preset row, shared across every picker. With no history the row is not rendered at all — so it can never be the line of empty boxes it was in the Content Studio.
  • One frame, not two. The popover drew a border and the picker drew another inside it. The picker is now borderless wherever the host already supplies the frame.
  • Pickers no longer run off the bottom of the screen. The Media Studio popover was placed from a hard-coded height estimate that VAR and the recent row invalidated; it now measures itself and moves back into view, and the Theme Styles picker opens upward when there is no room below.
  • Hue and alpha sliders are pinned to one height so they cannot stretch in the wider Variables panel, and the VAR list no longer overflows the picker.
  • Deleted 31 dead CSS rules aimed at a colour picker that no longer exists — CSS-only, never rendered, and exactly the kind of thing that makes “why does this look different” hard to answer.

v1.3.457 — VAR is back in the colour picker

  • VAR restored as the fifth format. Dropping it was wrong — ⚡ is a shortcut on a field, VAR is a mode of the picker. Selecting it swaps the channel fields for a searchable list of your MV variables and stores var(--token) instead of a literal. The bound token sits above the search with an unbind control, and the swatch shows the resolved colour.
  • Available in all four pickers. Media collection colours accepted six- or eight-digit HEX only; they now take a variable reference too, so a collection colour can follow a token instead of a frozen literal.
  • A shared variable cache means a picker host only has to say it can store a reference, instead of fetching its own copy of the list.

v1.3.456 — The flicker’s real cause, and OKLAB

  • The canvas flicker is fixed at the cause. Last build’s debounce only slowed it down. MV was writing Bricks’ store and posting the same payload to the canvas — and Bricks already mirrors every store write to the canvas itself, so the CSS regenerated twice per keystroke. MV now writes the store only, skips payloads that haven’t changed, and holds the panel re-render until the value settles.
  • OKLAB joins OKLCH in every picker. It is derived from the existing OKLCH conversion — the same colour in Cartesian rather than polar coordinates — so the two cannot drift apart, and HEX is unaffected.
  • Built the preset swatch row the Component Library has specified all along and no picker actually had.
  • “Backdrop behind panels” moved out of CSS Studio into Settings → General, beside Studio defaults. It controls nine modules and had no business living under CSS Studio.
  • One segmented control for the product, matching the Component Library’s. The backdrop intensity switch was inline-styled with its own geometry.

v1.3.455 — Live preview no longer leaks, and stops flickering

  • Closing MV without saving no longer leaves the edit in Bricks. The live preview writes to Bricks’ store, so an abandoned edit stayed on the canvas and in Bricks’ own panel after MV had already discarded it. The saved state is now put back on close, on Reset, and when the panel unmounts.
  • The canvas no longer flickers while you type. Every keystroke replaced the whole theme-styles map and re-rendered Bricks’ entire panel; pushes now coalesce to the pause between keystrokes and still read as live.
  • Theme Styles remembers the group you were last in, and switching styles no longer throws you back to General.
  • The Elements / Structure toolbar menu is withdrawn pending a redesign, and removed from installs that already had it. Dock, float and hide remain in MV Settings → Builder Panels.
  • Checklist audit: dropped two rows you confirmed working, one that outlived its feature, and one superseded by a later row testing the same thing.

Three mock prototypes are waiting on your decision — the box control (three options), per-control undo/redo/clear, and competing-CSS detection.

v1.3.454 — One colour picker, and Bricks’ panel keeps up

  • Bricks’ Theme Styles panel now updates with MV. The canvas was repainting, but the panel holds per-control state and showed the old values until you closed and reopened it. Bricks refreshes it by stamping rerenderControls on its store; MV now does the same after every change.
  • Every colour picker is one component again. The map, sliders, OKLCH fields and format tabs were already shared — but each host built its own footer and sized its own popover, which is why Variables, Theme Styles, Content Studio and Media Studio looked like four designs. Footers are now declared on the shared core and every host sizes from one width token.
  • The picker follows light mode. It had no light rules at all, so inside the Content Studio’s light canvas it rendered dark chrome — including the alpha checkerboard, which now uses light squares.
  • Swatches keep a 1:1 ratio and match the field height. The variables picker pinned its first column to 42px, so the swatch could never track the field beside it.
  • ⚡ opens a searchable dropdown of your MV variables with their resolved values, and an Unbind action when one is set. It used to just type var(-- into the field — and showed a second, redundant lightning icon next to the first.
  • Minimum canvas is removed and parked — the setting, its REST route, runtime and stored option are all gone. Nothing is left behind to migrate when it comes back.
  • Rewrote the Component Library’s colour picker entry, which still documented format tabs and a preset swatch row that no longer exist.

v1.3.453 — Theme styles apply live, no reload

Why nothing was happening: saving wrote the bricks_theme_styles option, but the builder generates its canvas CSS once at boot and never re-reads that option. The value was stored correctly and simply never reached the screen. MV now writes the builder store the way Bricks’ own panel does — the styles map first, then the active style’s settings, which is the watcher the canvas uses to regenerate. The custom stylesheet goes through the same path, so it applies too.

  • The canvas repaints on every field change, not only on Save — the same way Bricks previews its own theme style edits. Conditions are live as well: the server recomputes which styles apply to the page you are previewing on every read and write.
  • Minimum canvas now actually moves the canvas. Bricks’ watcher on the width lock only saves the number over AJAX; the preview width is recomputed only when a panel is resized. So setting 1600 stored 1600 and moved nothing until you resized something or reloaded. Bricks never hit this because its own padlock locks to the width you are already at. MV now mirrors the locked width onto the preview width, and restores the full width when you switch the lock off.
  • Colour picker: space above the Done button, a Clear command that removes the colour so the Bricks default applies again, and it closes when you click outside or press Escape.
  • ⚡ on every colour and text field opens the MV variable list. Suggestions previously appeared only once what you had typed already looked like a variable reference — which you had to know.
  • Branded the scrollbar on the CSS editor’s variable-suggestion list; it was still the browser default.

v1.3.452 — Theme Styles, complete and actually applied

The important part: Bricks reads a theme style as settings[group][key]. MV wrote every value flat, at the top level of settings. Bricks stored those keys and never read one of them, so apart from conditions, nothing MV saved here had any effect on the site. Every value is now written into the group Bricks reads it from, and values saved by older MV builds are lifted into place automatically the first time a style is opened.

  • Saving no longer deletes your element styles. MV replaced the whole settings array on save. A style also carries Bricks’ ~40 per-element groups (Section, Button, Heading…), and every one of them was wiped. Saves now merge, and the Elements tab lists exactly which element groups the style is carrying.
  • All nine whole-style groups, all 107 controls. General, Colors, Links, Contextual spacing, Content, Typography, Popup, Stylesheet and Conditions — group ids, keys, labels, placeholders, option tokens and show/hide rules are generated from Bricks’ own control files, not transcribed.
  • Real controls, no JSON textareas. Typography is a 15-field panel (family, weight, size, line-height, tracking, align, transform, decoration, white-space, text-wrap, variation settings, fallback, text shadow); border is width + style + colour; box-shadow is X/Y/blur/spread + colour + inset; spacing is the four-side box; multi-selects take custom tags; contextual-spacing targets are a repeater.
  • Values can bind to MV variables — any colour or text field accepts var(--token) with autocomplete from your own variables.
  • Groups are tabs, not a stack, each with a dot when it holds a value, so you can see what a style sets at a glance. H1–H6 is one level at a time instead of six near-identical blocks.
  • CSS selectors and stylesheets are stored byte-for-byte. They were passed through sanitize_textarea_field, which strips %xx sequences and anything tag-shaped — quietly corrupting CSS.
